levels.mom-dad:
Willowbrook Hollow is a hidden community of animals living in the woods, meadows, and streams behind the Willowbrook Animal Sanctuary. The animals speak to one another across species, but humans cannot understand them. The only human the Hollow knows is Zoe, the young helper at the sanctuary. To the animals she is a mysterious “giant” whose routines (boots, buckets, mismatched clothes, kind hands, and lately a squeaky viola) set the rhythm of their days.

The series is written for readers whose ideas are ahead of their decoding. The stories, jokes, and stakes are pitched at 8–10-year-olds, while the words follow strict decoding rules. That way a child who loves a good 4th-grade joke can read the book on their own, fluently, without the text feeling babyish.

How the Circles work: each Circle is both a rank in the Hollow and a reading level. What changes from Circle to Circle is how hard the words are to decode, not how grown-up the story is.
• Acorn (Newcomers): words of up to 2 syllables using closed, open, silent-e, vowel-team, and r-controlled syllables; short sentences; 1,000–2,000 words. Ceremony: green leaf charm.
• Leaf (Helpers): up to 3 syllables; adds consonant-le, soft c and g, igh, silent letters, and -tion; 2,000–4,000 words. Ceremony: carved twig token.
• Branch (Junior Rescuers): up to 4 syllables; adds ough and augh and Latin suffixes; connected subplots; 4,000–7,000 words. Ceremony: carved acorn pendant.
• Oak (Mentors): up to 5 syllables; roots and mild figurative language; parallel threads; 7,000–12,000 words. Ceremony: the Oaklight.
• Elder (Storytellers): no limits; multi-book arcs; 12,000–20,000 words. Ceremony: a carved staff at dawn.
A few high-frequency “heart words” (said, was, could) and a handful of highlighted “story words” per book (like viola) are allowed at every level.

Choosing a starting Circle: these books are for independent, enjoyable reading, so start one Circle below where your reader needs a teacher’s help. They should read about 98% of the words on a page without help. You can unlock any Circle in the Parent Corner.

Reading together in the app:
• Read to Me reads each page aloud and highlights each word, then says “Your turn!” This is echo reading.
• Tap any word to see it split into syllables and hear it said, all at once or slowly, one syllable at a time.
• Practice Read is a one-minute timed read of a chapter. Tap the last word read, add any missed words, and the app tracks words correct per minute against your reader’s own best, never against other children.
• Quizzes read every question aloud, allow unlimited tries, and include “what do you think?” questions with no wrong answer.
• Settings offer dyslexia-friendly fonts, larger text, roomier spacing, a reading ruler, high contrast, reduced motion, and voice speed.
• Progress and badges are saved on the device. Use the progress code in the Parent Corner to move them to another tablet, phone, or Chromebook.
levels.acorn:
Willowbrook Hollow is a secret place. It is in the woods behind the sanctuary. The critters there can talk to each other. People do not know!

When something new comes to the sanctuary, the friends go to see. They help. They make jokes. They get into a big mess, and then they fix it.

Circles are steps.

• Acorn is the first step.

• Each step has bigger words and longer stories.

When you finish the Acorn books, the whole Hollow has a party. You get a green leaf charm!
levels.leaf:
Willowbrook Hollow is a hidden town of animals behind the sanctuary.
They chatter, laugh, and help each other—while humans never notice.

New friends are welcomed kindly. The Hollow helps them heal, learn, and belong.

Circles show how everyone grows:
• Acorn: newcomers learning the basics.
• Leaf: helpers who join the work and discover funny side adventures.

At the end of Leaf, the Hollow celebrates. You receive a carved twig token and step forward.
levels.branch:
Willowbrook Hollow is busy with adventure. Friends secretly help one another behind the sanctuary fences.

Circles are steps of growing up:
• Acorn: the first welcome.
• Leaf: helpers at work.
• Branch: junior rescuers who face a big challenge and a smaller one at the same time.

Branch books add feeling words and short paragraphs to build strength for longer reading.
The Branch ceremony brings everyone together with a carved acorn pendant and cheerful speeches.
levels.oak:
Willowbrook Hollow is a place of learning. Animals plan kindly and help with care.

The path through the Circles:
• Acorn: first steps.
• Leaf: helping hands.
• Branch: junior rescuers.
• Oak: mentors who guide others and balance plans with laughter.

Oak books use richer description and gentle figurative language. They often tell two threads at once.
At Oak’s end, the Oaklight Ceremony glows with fireflies and carved pendants.
levels.elder:
The Elder Circle is rare. In the Hollow, it is the rank of storytellers and tradition‑keepers.

For readers, Elder books bring:
• longer word counts,
• multi‑book arcs,
• deeper emotional themes.

Elder ceremonies happen at dawn. Carved staffs are given, stories are shared, and gentle laughter carries into the new day.
By Elder, both reader and Hollow are strong—every step of reading has been a step of belonging.
